bibl.title: A new measure for functional similarity of gene products based on Gene Ontology

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A SIMILARITY MEASURE COMPUTED FROM A CONTROLLED VOCABULARY'S OWN SHAPE - how alike two gene products are, decided by where their Gene Ontology terms sit in the graph rather than by their sequences
span.quote: Gene products are functionally similar if they have comparable molecular functions and are involved in similar biological processes. These gene products did not necessarily evolve from a common ancestor and therefore do not necessarily show sequence similarity.

span.label: how to score the functional similarity of two gene products from their GO annotations alone, in a way that survives incomplete and partly subjective annotation
span.quote: In addition, GO is an ongoing project in which new terms are added continuously but many specific functional terms may still be missing. The manual mapping of GO terms to genes is based on results available in the scientific literature or in public databases, but relies on human decision and therefore is considerably subjective [ 12 ]. In addition, a large part of gene products is not yet annotated with GO terms.

span.label: two measures - simRel for a pair of GO terms and funSim for a pair of gene products - that combine Resnik's and Lin's definitions and allow partial matches
span.quote: The measure also allows for partial matches, resulting in a more robust similarity score for the comparison of gene products with incomplete annotation or for the comparison of multi-functional proteins.

span.label: method
span.quote: The measure also allows for partial matches, resulting in a more robust similarity score for the comparison of gene products with incomplete annotation or for the comparison of multi-functional proteins.

span.label: similarity of meaning treated as a computable property of a vocabulary's graph, with the vocabulary's own defects inherited by every score
span.quote: One problem is that the depth of a term in the GO graph is not representative of the specificity of the underlying concept. Different terms on the same rank (same depth in the GO graph) usually are not equally specific.

span.label: semantic similarity over the GO directed acyclic graph: information content of the lowest common ancestor, combined across the three ontologies, evaluated against sequence-similarity approaches and applied to yeast, human, fungal and Pfam sets
span.term: semantic similarity over the GO directed acyclic graph: information content of the lowest common ancestor, combined across the three ontologies, evaluated against sequence-similarity approaches and applied to yeast, human, fungal and Pfam sets
span.quote: Resnik [ 13 , 14 ] developed a measure of semantic similarity for "is-a" ontologies based on the information content of the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two terms. The more frequently a term occurs, i.e., the higher its probability of occurring, the lower its information content. If the LCA of two terms describes a generic concept, these terms are not very similar and this is reflected in a low information content of their LCA. This measure considers how specific the LCA of the two terms is but disregards how far away the two terms are from their LCA.

span.label: DEPTH IS NOT SPECIFICITY, AND THE MEASURE EXISTS BECAUSE OF IT: `the DEPTH OF A TERM in the GO graph IS NOT REPRESENTATIVE OF THE SPECIFICITY of the underlying concept. DIFFERENT TERMS ON THE SAME RANK (same depth in the GO graph) USUALLY ARE NOT EQUALLY SPECIFIC.` The obvious structural proxy for how precise a term is does not work, and information content is used instead
span.quote: One problem is that the depth of a term in the GO graph is not representative of the specificity of the underlying concept. Different terms on the same rank (same depth in the GO graph) usually are not equally specific.

span.label: AND THE MEASURE DOES NOT RETURN 1.0 FOR A TERM COMPARED WITH ITSELF: `Comparing the GO term `biotin biosynthesis` (GO:0009102) WITH ITSELF results in a sim Rel score of 0.99993. THE SCORE IS SMALLER THAN 1.0 BECAUSE sim Rel RELIES ON THE PROBABILITY OF THE TERM`. IDENTITY IS NOT A FIXED POINT OF THE MEASURE, and everything built on it inherits that - including the funSim score and the maps drawn from it
span.quote: Comparing the GO term "biotin biosynthesis" (GO:0009102) with itself results in a sim Rel score of 0.99993. The score is smaller than 1.0 because sim Rel relies on the probability of the term (see Methods for details).

span.label: AND THE INTERPRETIVE BANDS ARE CHOSEN, NOT DERIVED: `GO terms with a sim Rel score ABOVE 0.9 correspond to HIGHLY SIMILAR functions. BETWEEN 0.5 AND 0.7, the two GO terms MAY BE CONSIDERED FUNCTIONALLY RELATED and BELOW 0.3, THEY ARE NOT FUNCTIONALLY SIMILAR.` Three classes on a continuous score, with the ranges 0.3-0.5 and 0.7-0.9 left unnamed
span.quote: The sim Rel score ranges between 0 and 1. GO terms with a sim Rel score above 0.9 correspond to highly similar functions. Between 0.5 and 0.7, the two GO terms may be considered functionally related and below 0.3, they are not functionally similar.

span.label: AND THE THING BEING REPLACED HAS A MEASURED ERROR RATE: `Devos and Valencia suggest that UP TO 30% OF THE FUNCTION ANNOTATIONS MADE THROUGH SEQUENCE SIMILARITY SEARCHES MIGHT BE ERRONEOUS`, and the EC number `tends to be COMPLETELY CONSERVED ONLY FOR PROTEINS WITH MORE THAN 80% SEQUENCE IDENTITY ... PROBLEMATIC to assign EC numbers based on a sequence alignment with LESS THAN 30% IDENTITY`
span.quote: Devos and Valencia [ 2 , 3 ] suggest that up to 30% of the function annotations made through sequence similarity searches might be erroneous.

span.label: and the definition the whole apparatus serves is explicitly NOT evolutionary: `Gene products are FUNCTIONALLY SIMILAR IF they have COMPARABLE MOLECULAR FUNCTIONS AND ARE INVOLVED IN SIMILAR BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES. These gene products DID NOT NECESSARILY EVOLVE FROM A COMMON ANCESTOR and therefore DO NOT NECESSARILY SHOW SEQUENCE SIMILARITY`
span.quote: Gene products are functionally similar if they have comparable molecular functions and are involved in similar biological processes. These gene products did not necessarily evolve from a common ancestor and therefore do not necessarily show sequence similarity.

span.label: THE VOCABULARY IS INCOMPLETE AND THE MAPPING IS SUBJECTIVE, SAID BY ITS USERS: `GO is an ongoing project in which new terms are added continuously but MANY SPECIFIC FUNCTIONAL TERMS MAY STILL BE MISSING. The manual mapping of GO terms to genes ... RELIES ON HUMAN DECISION AND THEREFORE IS CONSIDERABLY SUBJECTIVE ... a LARGE PART of gene products IS NOT YET ANNOTATED with GO terms.`
span.quote: In addition, GO is an ongoing project in which new terms are added continuously but many specific functional terms may still be missing. The manual mapping of GO terms to genes is based on results available in the scientific literature or in public databases, but relies on human decision and therefore is considerably subjective [ 12 ]. In addition, a large part of gene products is not yet annotated with GO terms.

span.label: AND A NAMED MISSING ANNOTATION WITH ITS CONSEQUENCE: `such sequence-independent similarity measures are ALWAYS LIMITED BY THE AVAILABILITY AND QUALITY OF THE FUNCTIONAL ANNOTATIONS and their underlying ontologies. This is reflected by the previously mentioned MISSING `boron transport` ANNOTATION for the human protein Q8NBS3, MAKING IT IMPOSSIBLE TO FIND FUNCTIONALLY RELATED PROTEINS in yeast.` One absent term, one comparison that cannot be made
span.quote: Nevertheless, such sequence-independent similarity measures are always limited by the availability and quality of the functional annotations and their underlying ontologies. This is refected by the previously mentioned missing "boron transport" annotation for the human protein Q8NBS3 , making it impossible to find functionally related proteins in yeast.

span.label: NO GOLD STANDARD, AND THE PAPER SAYS WHAT THAT COSTS: `The comparison of our measures with Lord's approach IS LIMITED BY THE LACK OF A GOLD STANDARD for either TRUE POSITIVES OR TRUE NEGATIVES. Therefore, ONE IS RESTRICTED TO THE COMPARISON OF THE SHAPES OF THE DISTRIBUTIONS of scores.` `ainsworth2020`, staged in this corpus an hour before this record, says `NO CLEAR GOLD STANDARD EXISTS` about serological assays. Ontology similarity and immunoassays, fourteen years apart, blocked on the same missing thing
span.quote: The comparison of our measures with Lord's approach [ 16 ] is limited by the lack of a gold standard for either true positives or true negatives. Therefore, one is restricted to the comparison of the shapes of the distributions of scores.

span.label: and the remedy is named as an open problem rather than claimed: `FUTURE PROGRESS IN THIS AREA REQUIRES AN OBJECTIVE CRITERION FOR TESTING THE PERFORMANCE of the different measures of functional similarity`
span.quote: Future progress in this area requires an objective criterion for testing the performance of the different measures of functional similarity.

span.label: and the scope is stated as additive rather than replacing: `The new approach IS NOT INTENDED TO BE A REPLACEMENT of the sequence comparison or homology-based approaches BUT RATHER PROVIDES AN ADDITIONAL ALTERNATIVE for the objective comparison of the annotated gene products`
span.quote: The new approach is not intended to be a replacement of the sequence comparison or homology-based approaches but rather provides an additional alternative for the objective comparison of the annotated gene products.

span.label: DAMAGE INHERITED FROM THE PUBLISHER, NOT FROM OUR EXTRACTION: the staged body reads `refect` FOUR times and `reflect` THREE - a lost `fl` ligature - and BOTH COUNTS ARE IDENTICAL IN EUROPE PMC's OWN fullTextXML, checked directly. Second confirmed instance of Q-990's category and a different mechanism from the first: zook2016 lost a whole `<` and its following text, this loses one letter of a ligature. span.label: biological process
span.quote: The Gene Ontology (GO) is divided into three orthogonal ontologies, biological process , molecular function , and cellular component . The three ontologies are represented as directed acyclic graphs (DAG) in which nodes correspond to terms and their relationships are represented by edges. Each node can have several parents and several children. There are two types of relationships. "is-a" indicates that the child is a subclass of the parent, and "part-of" is used when the child is a component of the parent.
